{
  "participants": [
    {
      "login": "fanquake",
      "stance": "neutral",
      "note": "asked about squashing commits and file permission changes; moved PR to draft"
    },
    {
      "login": "maflcko",
      "stance": "neutral",
      "note": "noted rebase needs and silent merge conflict; investigated CI warning"
    },
    {
      "login": "luke-jr",
      "stance": "objection",
      "note": "requested changes on chain terminology, prefix handling, and unsupported vs invalid error wording"
    },
    {
      "login": "Sjors",
      "stance": "support",
      "note": "Concept ACK; tested individual commits, provided a fixup commit, and advised on commit structure"
    },
    {
      "login": "RandyMcMillan",
      "stance": "support",
      "note": "Approach ACK"
    },
    {
      "login": "achow101",
      "stance": "objection",
      "note": "objected to invalid Bech32 separator logic and to the maintenance burden of dynamically computing Base58 prefixes"
    },
    {
      "login": "rkrux",
      "stance": "support",
      "note": "Concept ACK; noted real-world debugging issues from unclear address/key network mismatch errors"
    },
    {
      "login": "jonatack",
      "stance": "support",
      "note": "Concept ACK"
    },
    {
      "login": "l0rinc",
      "stance": "objection",
      "note": "Concept ACK on intent, but requested changes blocking merge until commits are split into focused, reviewable refactors and behavior changes"
    },
    {
      "login": "sedited",
      "stance": "neutral",
      "note": "pinged reviewers for updates"
    }
  ],
  "claims": [
    {
      "id": "rc:1239033958",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "harm": "Error message incorrectly stated that address prefixes indicate a chain.",
      "quote": "The prefix does not necessarily indicate a chain. The current error is more correct.",
      "blocking": true,
      "status": "resolved",
      "author_replies": ["rc:1239533282"],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "settled_by_id": "rc:1239533282",
      "settled_by_quote": "This has been resolved by rewording the error message since you are correct addresses have prefixes not chains."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:1239034595",
      "kind": "interface",
      "harm": "User-facing errors exposed internal naming by referring to Bitcoin as mainnet.",
      "quote": "Bitcoin shouldn't be called \"mainnet\" in user-facing errors.",
      "blocking": true,
      "status": "resolved",
      "author_replies": ["rc:1239531230"],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "settled_by_id": "rc:1239531230",
      "settled_by_quote": "This has been resolved by adding a function to chaintype.cpp called ChainTypeToDisplayString. This decodes the ChainType Enum into user-facing strings. Including using 'Bitcoin' to reference mainnet"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:1276765179",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "harm": "Prefixes not recognized by the client were labeled invalid rather than unsupported.",
      "quote": "Could just as well still be unsupported, not invalid.",
      "blocking": false,
      "status": "resolved",
      "author_replies": ["rc:1277194218"],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "settled_by_id": "rc:1277194218",
      "settled_by_quote": "I have changed this to read Invalid or unsupported prefix... This has been resolved in b66e974ac8f21971602051c08df830d14cf3df7e"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:1566472098",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "harm": "Rejecting Bech32 strings with multiple '1's breaks valid addresses because '1' is allowed in the HRP.",
      "quote": "This is incorrect. 1 is an allowed character in the human readable part, hence a multiple separators check doesn't make sense.",
      "blocking": true,
      "status": "resolved",
      "author_replies": ["rc:1779998510"],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "settled_by_id": "rc:1779998510",
      "settled_by_quote": "Thank you for this insight, the faulty logic has been removed as a part of the rebase/refactor in the most recent commit."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:1567767610",
      "kind": "maintenance",
      "harm": "Dynamically calculating Base58 prefixes from version bytes creates unnecessary maintenance burden when static chainparams suffice.",
      "quote": "It seems a bit odd to me to do all of this work to compute these prefixes just for error messaging. ISTM it would be a lot simpler to just hard code them into chainparams anyways... Merging this code seems like an additional maintenance burden for very little gain.",
      "blocking": true,
      "status": "resolved",
      "author_replies": ["rc:1567835969", "rc:1779998302"],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "settled_by_id": "rc:1779998302",
      "settled_by_quote": "The choice to use chainparams to store the Base58 address prefixes has been utilized in the most recent pull. This solution simplifies the PR a noticeable amount."
    },
    {
      "id": "r:4137958021",
      "kind": "maintenance",
      "harm": "Bundling large refactors, moves, deletions, and behavior changes across commits impedes review and risks regressions.",
      "quote": "my biggest concern (unrelated changes intertwined in big commits and commit messages not explaining the change) is still unaddressed. I have a hard time reviewing this meaningfully - without redoing everything locally, which I would like to avoid.",
      "blocking": true,
      "status": "open",
      "author_replies": ["c:4283207812"],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "settled_by_id": "",
      "settled_by_quote": ""
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3109233352",
      "kind": "safety",
      "harm": "Using std::string_view instead of std::string in chainparams risks lifetime bugs.",
      "quote": "SSO should already make these cheap, let's use std::string instead. That's consistent with the rest of CChainParams and removes the potential lifetime footgun.",
      "blocking": false,
      "status": "open",
      "author_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "settled_by_id": "",
      "settled_by_quote": ""
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3109384777",
      "kind": "approach",
      "harm": "Reparsing the input string during validation causes redundant decoding passes.",
      "quote": "Do we really need to reparse str here? Could we instead have a single path that lowers up front to avoid duplicated work?",
      "blocking": false,
      "status": "open",
      "author_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "settled_by_id": "",
      "settled_by_quote": ""
    }
  ],
  "support": [
    {
      "id": "r:1618676862",
      "verdict": "Concept ACK",
      "reason": "Looks good to improve address decoding errors; inspected and tested commit range.",
      "substantive": true
    },
    {
      "id": "c:1741964735",
      "verdict": "Approach ACK",
      "reason": "Approach ACK",
      "substantive": false
    },
    {
      "id": "r:2598102040",
      "verdict": "Concept ACK",
      "reason": "Agrees with improving error messages when address decoding fails.",
      "substantive": true
    },
    {
      "id": "c:2676235043",
      "verdict": "",
      "reason": "In favour of better address error parsing after experiencing confusing errors when debugging network-inconsistent keys.",
      "substantive": true
    },
    {
      "id": "r:2635042631",
      "verdict": "Concept ACK",
      "reason": "Concept ACK",
      "substantive": false
    },
    {
      "id": "r:3027286087",
      "verdict": "Concept ACK",
      "reason": "We should indeed make the error messages more user friendly.",
      "substantive": true
    }
  ],
  "notes": "Initial record population. While there is broad Concept support, the PR is held in draft pending author rework to address l0rinc's request to separate behavioral changes from refactors into reviewable commits."
}
